name: @prabhixtechnologies/ui
description: Shared React UI primitives for Prabhix product webs.
//exports: dist, and there is no publishConfig that swaps it for src.
These three fields used to point at ./src/index.ts with a publishConfig block that pointed
at ./dist, the idea being that a `file:` link would compile the sources for free while a
published tarball served compiled output. npm does not do that. Its publishConfig overrides
npm *config* values -- registry, tag, access, provenance -- and overriding package.json
fields such as `exports` is a Yarn and pnpm feature. npm ignored the block silently, so
1.0.0 shipped pointing consumers at raw TypeScript, which Vite's Rollup build does not
transpile inside node_modules and Next needs `transpilePackages` for. Unpacking the
published tarball is what showed it; reading this file is what hid it.
One honest value is workable because of `prepare` below. npm runs that after any install
and before any pack, so dist exists for the gallery, for a typecheck and for a publish
alike, and the gallery photographs the artefact consumers actually receive.
preset.css deliberately stays on src. It is plain CSS, tsup copies it to dist byte for byte,
and src ships regardless: Tailwind v4 skips node_modules, so consumers point `@source` at
this package's src to find the primitives' class names. One tree rather than two.
//files: src is kept alongside dist so the published sourcemaps resolve to real sources when a
consumer steps into a primitive in the debugger.
The tests are excluded. They import @testing-library, axe-core and vitest, which are dev
dependencies here and absent in every consumer, so shipping them puts unresolvable imports
in the tarball -- harmless while nothing reaches for them and a confusing failure the moment
something does, such as a consumer's own test runner globbing node_modules.
//scripts: `prepare` runs tsup, which is what lets `exports` name dist and only dist. npm runs prepare
after every install -- including `npm ci` on a runner -- and again before any pack, so no
workspace here can import this package before it has been compiled, and no publish can ship
a dist older than src. dist/ is gitignored, so building it on install leaves the tree clean
and does not trip the "generated output is committed" gate in publish.yml.
//: Everything this package imports is a peer, and every consuming app must declare all of them.
That is not a style choice. Apps link this package with `file:`, and npm does not install a
linked package's own dependencies into the consumer - it assumes the link target's tree will
serve. Vite's build agrees, because it resolves through the symlink to the real path. Vitest
does not: it inlines linked sources and resolves from the link path, inside the app's own
node_modules. So a dependency declared only here resolves at build time and fails at test
time, which is the worst way for it to fail.
Peers are therefore the only declaration that actually reaches the apps. The cost is that
adding a primitive means adding its package in every app too, and the cost of forgetting
used to be a red test suite in an unrelated file. `check-peers.mjs` in @prabhixtechnologies/brand runs in
every repo's CI and fails with the exact npm command to run, so it is caught here instead.
react and react-dom are peers for the ordinary reason as well: hooks read a dispatcher off a
module-level singleton, and two copies fail as "Cannot read properties of null".
